subject.title: [Feature]: Self-evolving SOUL.md via opt-in reflection sub-turn + soul_update tool

question: Should OpenClaw accept a default-off core SOUL.md auto-evolution feature that lets a guarded reflection sub-turn write to SOUL.md, or should durable preference capture stay in memory/plugin surfaces?
rationale: The requested behavior is missing and has an implementation candidate, but it adds model-mediated writes to a prompt-loaded instruction file plus new config and CLI surfaces, so automation cannot choose the product and security boundary.

options.title: Accept guarded core SOUL updates
options.body: Keep this issue canonical and review the linked PR only after it uses private tool gating, send-policy ordering, visible notice/undo/provenance, and hostile-input coverage.

options.title: Move durable preferences to memory/plugins
options.body: Decline direct SOUL.md mutation in core and ask for the feature through memory plugins or a new plugin/API seam if current extension points are insufficient.

options.title: Decline automatic instruction mutation
options.body: Close this and the older overlapping request if maintainers do not want runtime/model-mediated writes to SOUL.md at all.

recommendation.title: Accept guarded core SOUL updates
recommendation.body: Keep this issue canonical and review the linked PR only after it uses private tool gating, send-policy ordering, visible notice/undo/provenance, and hostile-input coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision spans SOUL docs, prompt assembly, config policy, plugin boundaries, and the security posture reflected in the history above.
